Currently swsusp saves the contents of highmem pages by copying them to the
normal zone which is quite inefficient (eg.  it requires two normal pages
to be used for saving one highmem page).  This may be improved by using
highmem for saving the contents of saveable highmem pages.
Namely
column2: during the suspend phase of the suspend-resume cycle we try to

column1: allocate as many free highmem pages as there are saveable highmem pages.
If there are not enough highmem image pages to store the contents of all of
the saveable highmem pages
column2: some of them will be stored in the ""normal""

column1: memory.  Next
column2: we allocate as many free ""normal"" pages as needed to store

column1: the (remaining) image data.  We use a memory bitmap to mark the allocated
free pages (ie.  highmem as well as ""normal"" image pages).
Now
column2: we use another memory bitmap to mark all of the saveable pages

column1: (highmem as well as ""normal"") and the contents of the saveable pages are
copied into the image pages.  Then
column2: the second bitmap is used to save the

column1: pfns corresponding to the saveable pages and the first one is used to save
their data.
During the resume phase the pfns of the pages that were saveable during the
suspend are loaded from the image and used to mark the ""unsafe"" page
frames.  Next
column2: we try to allocate as many free highmem page frames as to

column1: load all of the image data that had been in the highmem before the suspend
and we allocate so many free ""normal"" page frames that the total number of
allocated free pages (highmem and ""normal"") is equal to the size of the
image.  While doing this we have to make sure that there will be some extra
free ""normal"" and ""safe"" page frames for two lists of PBEs constructed
later.

other list of PBEs is for the copies of highmem suspend pages.  The pages
in this list are restored (in a reversible way) right before the
